stories.title: Construction of a leak detection and pressure regulation system for municipal water distribution networks integrating digital twin technology
stories.description: Aging municipal water networks lose a substantial share of treated water to leakage, yet detection and pressure control are still pursued on separate models, so neither can inform the other. This paper builds an integrated system in which both functions read from and write to one continuously synchronized digital twin. The twin couples an open-source hydraulic kernel, a pressure-dependent demand closure and emitter-based leakage to an ensemble Kalman filter and a weighted least-squares recalibration step, so that heads, flows, Hazen–Williams roughness coefficients and demand multipliers are updated from multi-source telemetry rather than frozen at commissioning. Detection normalizes twin residuals against diurnal demand patterns and combines a sliding-window CUSUM statistic with a Mahalanobis joint test; the residual field then feeds a graph attention network that scores each junction and aggregates node posteriors into ranked suspect pipe segments. Regulation solves a bi-objective program over valve settings and pump speeds, weighting nodes by their leak posterior so that head is reduced hardest where water actually escapes, subject to service-head, switching and resilience constraints. Results are reported network by network rather than pooled alone. The pooled F1 reaches 0.916 and the Top-5 hit rate 0.816, against 0.836 and 0.573 for the strongest baseline, with per-network F1 ranging from 0.903 on C-Town to 0.932 on Net3 and mean detection latency falling to roughly four hours. On the official BattLeDIM 2019 scenarios, held out as an independent validation set, the same model retains an F1 of 0.818 but sheds about twenty points of Top-5 hit rate, which bounds how far the in-house training distribution generalizes. Closing the loop on C-Town raises leakage reduction from 24.6% under uniform depressurization to 37.5% while holding service compliance at 99.4%. Ablations identify state assimilation as the load-bearing component. Code and result records accompany the paper; scalability beyond a few thousand nodes, transient hydraulics and the capital cost of dense instrumentation remain open limitations.

stories.title: Deficiency of non-muscle myosin IIA promotes neuroinflammation by impairing autophagic degradation of VCAM-1 in brain endothelium
stories.description: Endothelial cell dysfunction is a major driver of neuroinflammation, a critical contributor to neurological disorders. Non-muscle myosin IIA (NMIIA), a key cytoskeletal protein, has been implicated in cerebrovascular pathology, but its role in endothelial-mediated neuroinflammation remains unclear. This study reveals that NMIIA expression is downregulated in brain microvascular endothelial cells during aging. Using in vitro knockdown and endothelial-specific conditional knockout mouse models, we demonstrate that NMIIA deficiency specifically upregulates VCAM-1 protein without affecting its mRNA or other inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, NMIIA loss impairs autophagic flux, particularly the autophagosome-lysosome fusion, leading to inhibited autophagic degradation and subsequent accumulation of VCAM-1. Proteomic analysis and biochemical assays identified Caveolin-1 (Cav-1) as a direct binding partner of NMIIA. NMIIA deficiency promotes the redistribution of the autophagy-related protein ATG5 into Cav-1-enriched lipid raft domains, a process known to suppress autophagy initiation. Functionally, soluble VCAM-1 released from NMIIA-deficient endothelial cells promotes pro-inflammatory polarization of microglia and induces neuronal apoptosis in vitro. In vivo, NMIIA iECKO mice exhibit increased microglial activation, impaired hippocampal neurogenesis, neuronal loss, and significant deficits in learning and memory behaviors. Collectively, our findings define a novel NMIIA–Cav-1–autophagy–VCAM-1 regulatory axis in brain endothelium, positioning NMIIA as a crucial maintainer of neurovascular homeostasis by preventing VCAM-1-driven neuroinflammation. This pathway provides new mechanistic insights into aging-related cerebrovascular dysfunction and offers potential therapeutic targets for neuroinflammatory diseases.

stories.title: Parental attitudes toward myopia prevention: insights from an Australian survey
stories.description: Prevention or delay of myopia onset has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce the long-term burden of myopia and associated ocular complications. However, little is known about parental awareness of myopia and acceptance of interventions aimed at preventing myopia onset in children. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Australian parents and guardians of children aged 4–18 years. Participants completed questions assessing myopia awareness, knowledge, personal and child myopia status, and willingness to participate in pre-myopia intervention programs. Associations between participant characteristics and willingness to engage in pre-myopia intervention were evaluated using multivariable ordinal logistic regression. A total of 800 responses were included in the analysis. Participants with myopia and those with a myopic child demonstrated significantly greater myopia awareness and knowledge than other participants. Overall willingness to consider pre-myopia intervention was high, with 76.8% of participants responding Yes, 19.5% Maybe, and 3.8% No. Greater myopia knowledge was independently associated with increased willingness to participate in pre-myopia intervention (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.25–1.43, p < 0.001). Participants with both myopic and non-myopic children demonstrated lower willingness compared with participants with no myopic children. Cost, evidence of treatment effectiveness, and recommendation from an eye-care professional were the most influential factors affecting participation and adherence to intervention. Australian parents demonstrated high willingness to engage in pre-myopia interventions. Myopia knowledge was the strongest independent predictor of willingness, whereas direct experience with myopia was not. These findings suggest that improving parental understanding of myopia may be critical for successful implementation of future pre-myopia prevention programs in Western populations.

stories.title: Depth-dependent inter-pixel distance in trench-isolated LGADs for shallow radiation detection
stories.description: The fill factor of finely segmented low-gain avalanche detectors (LGAD) is limited by the effective inter-pixel distance (IPD), particularly when charge is generated far from the gain layer. In this work, 200 $$\mu $$m thick trench-isolated LGADs (TI-LGADs) fabricated by Micron Semiconductor Ltd. were characterized using single-photon and two-photon absorption transient current technique measurements at ELI Beamlines to determine the dependence of IPD on interaction depth, illumination direction, and gain-layer doping. The measurements show that the effective IPD is smallest near the trench side of the device and increases as charge generation occurs deeper in the sensor bulk, with a minimum measured IPD of approximately 7 $$\mu $$m. Devices with higher gain-layer doping exhibit larger IPD, indicating a trade-off between gain and effective fill factor, while depth-resolved measurements reveal enhanced charge collection at the trench edge consistent with a localized high-field region at the gain-layer/trench interface. These results show that, in thick TI-LGADs, back-side shallow absorption corresponds to charge generation far from the multiplication region and can therefore lead to an increased IPD, which may limit the performance of small-pixel designs. The findings identify an important design constraint for TI-LGADs intended for applications involving shallow energy deposition under back-side illumination.

stories.title: Privacy-accuracy trade-off optimization in sensitive surveys through regression estimation
stories.description: Collecting reliable information on sensitive quantitative characteristics remains a big challenge in social and behavioral surveys, as respondents often hesitate to answer truthfully. The Randomized Response Technique (RRT) helps protect privacy, but many existing models do not balance privacy and efficiency well. To resolve this problem, this study proposes a novel regression estimator designed to accurately estimate the sensitive population mean. The strength of this approach lies in incorporating non-sensitive auxiliary variables into data collected under strict privacy protocols. To thoroughly evaluate the behavior of this estimator, we apply it to data collected through existing distinct randomized response models. Theoretically, the proposed regression estimator is unbiased and benefits from a straightforward, closed-form variance expression, allowing for practical application. We assess privacy protection using a deviation-based metric, while efficiency is assessed through in terms of sampling variance. To capture the overall performance of the models, we also employ unified, weighted, and log-weighted composite measures that balance both privacy and precision. Extensive numerical examples and Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that the proposed estimator usually has lower variance and offers a better balance between privacy and efficiency than other existing mean estimators. These results indicate that the proposed estimator provides a practical, efficient, and privacy-preserving tool for surveys involving sensitive quantitative data.

stories.title: VDAC1 regulates disulfidptosis susceptibility and associates with the immune microenvironment via multi-omics analysis in lung adenocarcinoma
stories.description: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the predominant subtype of non‑small cell lung cancer, continues to exhibit high incidence and mortality due to tumor heterogeneity and therapy resistance, underscoring the need for novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study aimed to systematically characterize the expression, prognostic value, immune‑microenvironment modulation, and functional role of VDAC1 in LUAD, with a focus on its regulation of glucose‑deprivation–induced disulfidptosis. By integrating multi‑omics data from public resources, we performed differential expression, copy‑number variation, survival, immune‑infiltration, pathway‑enrichment, and single‑cell/spatial transcriptomic analyses. Findings were validated using immunohistochemistry on 15 paired LUAD samples and functional assays in A549 and PC‑9 cell lines. VDAC1 was significantly upregulated at mRNA and protein levels in LUAD, and its high expression correlated with poor prognosis and therapy resistance. Genomic copy‑number amplification and promoter hypomethylation cooperatively drove VDAC1 overexpression. Single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics confirmed VDAC1 enrichment specifically in malignant epithelial cells. Immune‑microenvironment analysis revealed a positive correlation with antigen presentation and a negative correlation with CD4 + T‑cell recruitment, suggesting a role in fostering an immunosuppressive niche. Pathway analysis linked VDAC1 to pro‑tumor processes including cell‑cycle progression, hypoxia response, and DNA‑damage repair. Transcriptomic analysis further showed that VDAC1-high tumors were preferentially enriched for disulfidptosis core genes—including SLC7A11—distinguishing this program from ferroptosis and apoptosis. Functionally, VDAC1 knockdown suppressed cystine uptake, partially restored GSH/GSSG balance and NADPH levels, attenuated mitochondrial ROS accumulation, and ameliorated ultrastructural damage, thereby alleviating glucose‑deprivation–triggered disulfidptosis. In summary, this integrated multi‑omics and experimental study establishes VDAC1 as both an independent adverse prognostic factor and a key regulator of disulfidptosis in LUAD, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for selectively inducing tumor cell death.
